title: Native Interoperability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Native Interoperability”?
options: Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
questions.answer_key: Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Native Interoperability”?
options: Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Native Interoperability”?
options: Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Native Interoperability removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
questions.answer_key: Native Interoperability removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Native Interoperability removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
